fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: October brought 165,000 jobs against 65,000 forecast and a 0.3% rise in core prices, and the committee's hawks have gone public: Logan wants two more hikes, possibly rapidly, and Schmid says there is more work to do. The question for Warsh's Fed is whether to move by 50 bps, and how to say so.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US hosts a table whose members spent this month routing trade around it: Lula, Carney and Albanese converged on Manila chasing deals with Southeast Asia as a hedge against Trump's tariffs. The Kremlin, meanwhile, has floated a Putin-Xi-Trump summit, a three-way track that runs outside the twenty.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Eurozone inflation has run above 2% for eight straight months, and Nagel has backed a third ECB hike this year. The council decides while its leadership is in flux: Lagarde leaves on 7 February, Knot and De Cos are the two candidates to succeed her, and Germany is still stalling a deal on the vacant executive board seats.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: Britain's central bank hiked unanimously last month and forecast inflation peaking at 4.9%. Bailey then said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on, and the Bank's chief economist has since called for further rises. This meeting settles whether the war's price pressure has lasted long enough to meet Bailey's own condition.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: The board meets with the yen through 160 per dollar, even after Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day and Washington sold $500 million of euros for yen. Intervention buys time, but the rate is the lever the Bank of Japan holds, and Fed officials calling for more hikes are widening the gap from the other side.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-11-17.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly early estimate of what US retailers and restaurants sold. Consumer spending drives most of the American economy, so the figure moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for interest rates.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-11-17.recent: The Census Bureau publishes its latest count of US retail sales, the first hard read on household spending for the month it covers. It settles whether shoppers kept spending, which is the question the rest of the economy's demand picture rests on.

fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reports US GDP, settling how fast the world's largest economy grew in the quarter, and gives the Fed a measured number rather than a forecast to weigh.

fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending, which carries the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It sets the inflation read that rate expectations and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes the latest US PCE figures, covering household spending and the prices behind it for the most recent month. The release settles whether consumer inflation cooled or firmed, and whether spending held up.
